messages:
mira: quick heads-up — kernel 6.5 rolled to eu-central during the maintenance window, and we're seeing a bunch of GPU probe failures on the p4s and a few p100 hosts.

cory: logs?

mira: pasted the most common dmesg snippet from 3 hosts: 
```
[    3.672345] nvidia: probe deferred
[    3.673001] nvidia: failed to initialize, aborting
[    3.673450] nvidia: vfio: can't map BAR0
[    3.674000] pci 0000:65:00.0: BAR 0: can't reserve mem
```

jonah: also seeing NCCL handshake warnings in job logs — multiple workers drop during all-reduce with timeouts. Example from training job: `NCCL WARN NET/Socket : Connect error, peer 10.0.45.12: sid 42`

dana: impact: Autoscaler reports ~18 nodes NotReady across the eu-central GPU ASGs, new provisioning backlog for p4 capacity, some tenant jobs stuck in pending. Tracking shows 22% drop in usable GPU capacity for that region.

mira: initial triage: kernel 6.5 changes pci resource allocations + vfio handling; combined with driver bundle we ship for CUDA 11.8 (driver 525) looks like an ABI mismatch. I tried modprobe nvidia and modprobe nvidia_uvm: modprobe exits nonzero.

cory: can we hotpatch driver on a canary node?

jonah: tested locally on a spare host: installing driver 535.54.03 allowed the module to load under 6.5; with 525 it fails. So the regression is driver<->kernel, not NCCL itself. NCCL errors are downstream from missing / partially initialized devices.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance: rolling image update eu-central-1b — completed 06/12 02:17 UTC :white_check_mark:

dana: short-term mitigation options: 
- pin kernel to 5.15 for GPU ASGs (image rollback)
- or roll forward driver to 535 variant in the images (needs CI validation)
- taint newly upgraded nodes to prevent scheduling until validated

mira: plan proposed: 1) taint remaining 6.5-upgraded ASGs to stop scheduling, 2) create a small canary ASG with kernel 6.5 + driver 535 and run stress tests, 3) if canary passes, bake new image and push; otherwise roll ASGs back to 5.15 image.

cory: agree. For rollback we'll use the existing image-family snapshot from May (linux-5.15-gpu-v20240510). Rolling back ASGs should be < 90m if we scale gradually.

jonah: note: for on-host mitigation we can run `sudo apt-mark hold linux-image*` on critical nodes to prevent accidental upgrades, and use `dkms status` to check modules. Example commands: 
```bash
sudo apt-mark hold linux-image-generic
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced || true
dkms status | grep nvidia
```

dana: cost note — if we run fallback by overprovisioning older instance types for capacity while we bake images, expect ~+18% hourly spend in eu-central for 12–24h window. Ops budget signed off for emergency but want explicit approval to burst.

mira: approved to burst to maintain SLAs. I'll start canary ASAP and post results.

cory: assigning actions: @mira run canary + report back, @jonah prepare driver 535 test matrix (CUDA 11.8/12.1 combos), @dana open incident and notify sales if any customer latencies exceed 1h. I'll draft rollback playbook.

mira: starting canary now — will attach results in this thread. If anyone sees weird host-level panics, ping infra-oncall. :pray: 

infra-bot: Incident created — INC-20260612-17 (priority P2) — linked to this thread.

jonah: preliminary canary logs after driver swap look good: modules load, nvidia-smi reports GPUs, small NCCL all-reduce completed. Still validating long-run GPU memory stress.

mira: update 03:00 UTC — canary stable for 45m, moving to bake image. Will block the rollout until image is on CI and e2e passes.

cory: good. Follow-up items: add kernel+driver compatibility test to pre-merge CI for image builds, and add a healthcheck that verifies module probe post-upgrade before untainting.

mira: noted. Closing interim updates; will post bake artifact IDs here when ready.
